text:
Maya Chen: Heads-up — I'm preparing a canary for a new runtime config: `quarantine_quota`. Goal: soft-enforce small per-route quotas for newly onboarded routes to catch regressions early without hard-failing traffic. Proposal below, want quick sanity check before I open the console rollout.
Maya Chen: config sketch:
```json
{
  "name": "quarantine_quota",
  "mode": "soft",            // soft = throttles with advisory headers, not 5xx
  "percent": 2,                 // start at 2% of traffic
  "window_s": 60,               // quota window
  "tokens": 100,                // per-window tokens for new routes
  "telemetry_gate": "p95_latency_ms < 120 && error_rate < 0.5"
}
```

Jonah Patel: Nice. Two quick Qs: (1) Where do we evaluate the gate expression? client-side in the SDK or server-side in the config service? (2) How do we surface advisory headers so apps can opt-in to degrade gracefully?

Akiko Sato: +1 on server-side eval. If we do client-side, every SDK version becomes a rollout vector. Server-side lets us centralize logic and roll back faster. We should cache evaluation results for ~30s to avoid spiking config service.

Sam Ortiz: Server-side sounds right. Also: telemetry gating needs a control population. If the p95 is calculated across whole cluster we can get false positives when noisy routes spike. Suggest we compute the gate on the canary cohort only (the 2%). Use a shadow metric stream in the console so SREs can inspect before widening.

Priya Nair: Console UX notes: expose three things on the flag page — (1) current cohort percent, (2) shadow metrics (p50/p95/err) for canary vs baseline, (3) quick rollback button with optional annotation. Add an "adhoc bump" that requires a second approver if >5%. Also show advisory header example and a small snippet for app teams to treat the header: `X-Quota-Soft: used=37/100`

Jonah Patel: About advisory headers — they should be lineage-safe and stable. I propose namespacing them: `X-Redwood-Quota-Soft`. And add a small sample for how apps should react (degrade non-critical features first).

Maya Chen: Good call on namespacing. Ops question: if the telemetry gate trips, do we auto-rollback or pause and notify? I lean pause + notify + auto-rollback only if error_rate > 2% for 5m. Thoughts?

Akiko Sato: Pause + notify is safer. Auto-rollback for high error spikes is ok but needs a cooldown so flapping doesn't keep toggling. Also add a dry-run mode where the canary only logs quota hits in shadow (no throttling) for the first 10 minutes.

Priya Nair: Addendum to UX: in dry-run show an "impact estimator" that simulates quota hit rate and estimated p95 shift based on historical traces. Even a rough estimate helps PMs decide to proceed.

Sam Ortiz: Implementation note for infra: evaluation must be O(1) per request and avoid allocations. We can piggyback on existing routing middleware and keep the KV for per-route token counts in a sharded in-memory store. TTLs + consistent hashing.

Jonah Patel: One more internal-api debate: Should the config-service return the whole evaluated policy blob per-request, or just a token (policy_id, version) and the runtime has the blob cached? Blob per-request is simpler but bigger; token+cache reduces traffic but requires cache invalidation semantics. I prefer token+cache with an `etag`-style invalidation pushed on rollouts.

Maya Chen: Token+cache + push invalidation seems best. We'll implement a small SSE/stream to clients and a fallback long-poll for older SDKs. Add a debug endpoint to dump active policies for a route.

config-bot: Canary rollout started: `quarantine_quota` @ 2% cohort on cluster us-west-2. Monitoring stream: https://observability/redwood/quarantine_quota/canary/3034567890 :eyes:

Maya Chen: I'll open a short PR for the runtime changes and a console PR for the flag page. I'll also add the dry-run and advisory header examples. If nobody objects in the next hour I'll kick off the canary in the console and ping SRE for watch. :+1:
